canonical_question: Does the 'nearly linear response' of the {310} grains at elevated temperatures imply that plasticity has not yet initiated in those specific orientations despite the increased anisotropy?

question_variants.question: Does the 'nearly linear response' of the {310} grains at elevated temperatures imply that plasticity has not yet initiated in those specific orientations despite the increased anisotropy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence notes the nearly linear response of {310} grains at elevated temperatures but does not explicitly interpret this linearity as proof that plasticity has not initiated. While linearity often implies elasticity, the text does not make the direct causal link requested regarding the onset of plasticity in those specific orientations.

answers.answer: The text observes the nearly linear response but does not explicitly state that this implies the absence of plasticity initiation.
answers.measurement_outcome: the {310} grains undergo the second largest elastic strain with a nearly linear response.
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit statement linking linearity to the non-initiation of plasticity in {310} grains.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
